'''''Muscari armeniacum''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the squill [[subfamily]] Scilloideae of the asparagus [[family (botany)|family]] Asparagaceae (formerly the lilies, Liliaceae). It is a [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]] with basal, simple [[leaf|leaves]] and short flowering stems. It is one of a number of species and genera known as '''grape hyacinth''', in this case '''Armenian grape hyacinth'''<ref>{{Citation |last1=Grey-Wilson |first1=Christopher |last2=Mathew |first2=Brian |last3=Blamey |first3=Marjorie |year=1981 |title=Bulbs : the bulbous plants of Europe and their allies |location=London |publisher=Collins |isbn=978-0-00-219211-8 |name-list-style=amp}}, p. 115</ref> or '''garden grape-hyacinth'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> The flowers are purple, blue (with a white fringe), white (cv. 'Album') or pale pink (cv. 'Pink Sunrise') and the plants are usually {{convert|15|cm|in|0}} tall. ''M. armeniacum'' blooms in mid-Spring (April or May in the [[Northern Hemisphere]]) for 3–4 weeks. Some selections are fragrant. Established bulbs leaf in the autumn. 
''M. armeniacum'' is widespread in the woods and meadows of the Eastern [[Mediterranean]], from [[Greece]] and [[Turkey]] to the [[Caucasus]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/muscari |title=Muscari |publisher=Pacific Bulb Society |date=2013-04-24 |access-date=2013-10-03}}</ref> including [[Armenia]] which gives it its name.
[[File:Grape Hyacinth - Muscari armeniacum - Traubenhyazinthe - 01.jpg|thumb|upright|Flower details]]

==Cultivation==
''Muscari armeniacum'' is one of the most commonly cultivated species of ''Muscari'', is robust and naturalises easily.<ref name=Mathew1987>{{Citation |last=Mathew |first=Brian |year=1987 |title=The Smaller Bulbs |location=London |publisher=B.T. Batsford |isbn=978-0-7134-4922-8 }}, pp. 126</ref> It appeared in European gardens in 1871.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.paghat.com/muscariarmeniacum.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051024085130/http://www.paghat.com/muscariarmeniacum.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=October 24, 2005 |title=Paghat's Garden: Armenian Grape Hyacinth |publisher=Paghat.com |date= |access-date=2013-10-03}}</ref>

Cultivars listed by Mathew include 'Blue Spike' and 'Cantab'.<ref name=Mathew1987/> Others include 'Argaei Album' and 'Album' (white), 'Côte d'Azur', 'Dark Eyes, 'Early Giant', 'Fantasy Creation', 'Peppermint', 'Saffier', 'Valerie Finnis' (pale blue), and 'Pink Sunrise' (pale pink). The commonly available form is often referred to as ''M. armeniacum'' 'Blue'.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theplantexpert.com/springbulbs/Muscari.html |title=The Plant Expert: Muscari |access-date=2010-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091125215925/http://www.theplantexpert.com/springbulbs/Muscari.html |archive-date=2009-11-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/Muscari |title=Pacific Bulb Society |publisher=Pacific Bulb Society |date=2013-04-24 |access-date=2013-10-03}}</ref>

'Blue Spike' is a double flowered variety, with double florets on the flower stalk.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://northernshade.ca/2010/05/30/blue-muscari-and-pink-tulip-flowers/ |title=Northern Shade Gardening: Blue Muscari |publisher=Northernshade.ca |date= |access-date=2013-10-03}}</ref>
'Cantab' is pale blue. 
'Fantasy Creation' is a [[Sport (botany)|sport]] (a naturally occurring genetic mutation) of 'Blue Spike'.
<ref>{{cite web|url=http://home.tiscali.nl/hennessy/Fantasy%20Creation.htm |title=Martin Philippo: Muscaripages - Fantasy Creation |publisher=Home.tiscali.nl |date= |access-date=2013-10-03 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110614011030/http://home.tiscali.nl/hennessy/Fantasy%20Creation.htm |archivedate=2011-06-14}}</ref> 'Atlantic' is light blue, introduced by [[Jan van Bentem]] in 2002, by hybridisation in 1990 from ''M. armeniacum'' and an unknown parent.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://home.tiscali.nl/~hennessy/Atlantic.htm |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090814162413/http://home.tiscali.nl/~hennessy/Atlantic.htm |archivedate=2009-08-14 |title=Muscari armeniacum "Atlantic' }}</ref>
